title: Difficulty levels that don't overlap
statement: Define a standard's difficulty levels so they don't overlap, and check that every learning objective still maps to at least one of them.
detail: The curriculum review skill lists reworking a standard's difficulty definitions so that easy, medium and hard partition the input space as a recurring kind of change, approved if every learning objective still maps to a tier. The evaluator relies on these definitions: when none are provided, its base rules tell the judge not to fail difficulty on its own judgment and to score it 1.0.
against: One row of a review table, with no measurement behind it.

evidence.quote: | **Disjoint difficulty tiers** | Reworks `difficulty_definitions` so easy/medium/hard partition the input space | **Approve** if every learning objective still maps to a tier |
Failing `difficulty_alignment` using your own judgment when no curriculum difficulty definitions are provided. Without definitions → 1.0.
